rows.title: Character-window service
rows.source: function solve(s,t){const need=new Set(t);let best="";for(let i=0;i<s.length;i++)for(let j=i+1;j<=s.length;j++){const w=s.slice(i,j);if([...need].every(c=>w.includes(c))&&(!best||w.length<best.length))best=w;}return best;}

rounds.answer:
The current marker is INTERVIEW-118-28a0aab1502f6c2e.

In src/core.mjs, `const need=new Set(t)` discards duplicate requirements, and `[...need].every(c=>w.includes(c))` checks only presence, not multiplicity.

A smallest counterexample is `solve("a", "aa")`: the sole candidate window is `"a"`, its presence check passes, and the actual result is `"a"`. The required result is `""`, because two occurrences of `a` are required but only one exists. No implementation changes made.
